paper_metadata.title: Implementing Quantum Generative Adversarial Network (qGAN) and QCBM in Finance

summary: The paper reports two gate-based quantum machine learning experiments on IBM Qiskit simulators: a qGAN for Binance-derived option-pricing uncertainty using 5 crypto assets, 3 qubits per feature, 2000 training epochs, and a QCBM with 5 layers and optimizer comparison across Cobyla, SPSA, and Nelder-Mead. The qGAN loss converged to about 0.6931 at equilibrium, and the QCBM’s SPSA result was described as close to the real distribution, but no practical quantum advantage or real-hardware benchmark is demonstrated.

experiments.description: qGAN for learning/loading a real-world Binance-derived financial distribution for option-pricing uncertainty using a 1-qubit target state and a classical discriminator.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Financial samples from 5 crypto-asset series discretized into 32 values per feature using 3 qubits per feature; qGAN learns the target distribution over the discretized data.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Train generator to match the target data distribution and fool the discriminator; discriminator minimizes binary classification loss between real and generated samples.

problem_instance.description: Option-pricing uncertainty model using real Binance crypto market data.

dataset_specification.preprocessing: Discard samples below 5th percentile and above 95th percentile; discretize each feature into 32 values using 3 qubits per feature.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Loaded real-life data via Binance API; removed extreme tails (below 5th percentile and above 95th percentile) to reduce qubit requirements; mapped samples from multivariate normal distribution to discrete values; verified discretization with histograms.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Training over 2000 epochs; fidelity and generator/discriminator loss curves inspected.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: PyTorch tensor conversion and data loader creation; discretization of training data; histogram verification.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Fidelity analysis and comparison of generator/discriminator loss curves.

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: generator and discriminator losses intersect at Nash equilibrium; fidelity increases with iterations

speedup_claims.conditions: on the Binance-derived option-pricing uncertainty dataset in simulation
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper does not provide a numeric iteration count for the classical GAN, so the speedup is qualitative only.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: A larger, hardware-validated qGAN with explicit qubit counts, circuit depth, and scaling analysis; the paper only reports a 1-qubit target state, 5 assets, 3 qubits per feature, 2000 epochs, and simulator execution.
limiting_factors: Classical discriminator and classical preprocessing dominate the workflow
No classical baseline metrics are reported for a direct performance comparison

notes: Hardware inferred as simulator_other because the paper states the work was run on IBM Qiskit Aer / simulator environment and no real QPU device is named.

Num_qubits not explicitly stated for the full qGAN circuit; only 3 qubits per feature and 5 features are reported, but the paper does not clearly state the total register size used in the final circuit.
Speedup order is not characterized asymptotically; the paper only claims fewer iterations than classical GAN in practice.
The authors state qGAN 'promises' future quantum advantage, but the reported results are simulator-based and do not demonstrate practical advantage.

experiments.description: QCBM trained on the same Binance-derived financial dataset to approximate the target probability distribution, with optimizer comparison across Cobyla, SPSA, and Nelder-Mead.

algorithm.variant: Quantum Circuit Born Machine (QCBM) with interleaving layers
algorithm.ansatz: interleaving circuit with repeated odd/even layers
algorithm.convergence_criteria: optimization over 5 layers; no explicit stopping criterion reported

hyperparameters.epsilon: small positive perturbation ε in modified cost function

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Probability distribution over discrete outcomes learned by a parametrized quantum circuit; the paper does not specify a qubit-to-variable mapping beyond the circuit-based distribution model.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Minimize cost function C(θ) = -(1/d) Σ_d ln(P(x_d)) or modified form C(θ)=-(1/d) Σ_d ln(max(ε, P_θ(x_d))).

problem_instance.description: Distribution learning on the same real Binance financial dataset used for qGAN.

dataset_specification.preprocessing: Histogram used to verify state-vector characteristics; same dataset as qGAN section.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: The paper states the same real-life Binance data were used; details beyond histogram verification are not further specified for QCBM.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Optimizer comparison (Cobyla vs SPSA vs Nelder-Mead) and comparison of learned/simulated distribution against real distribution.

implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Comparison of real and simulated distributions; optimizer performance comparison.

speedup_claims.caveats: The paper reports only a qualitative optimizer comparison and distribution matching; no speedup claim is made.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: A larger-scale, hardware-backed QCBM study with explicit qubit counts, circuit depth, and scaling/crossover analysis; the paper only reports a 5-layer circuit and simulator-based optimizer comparison.
limiting_factors: No classical baseline with quantitative metrics
Results are limited to distribution matching on simulator

notes: Hardware inferred as simulator_other because the paper reports Qiskit simulator usage and does not name a real QPU.
Num_qubits is not explicitly stated for the QCBM circuit in the provided text; only the 5-layer circuit structure is reported.
Speedup order is not characterized asymptotically; the paper only reports empirical distribution matching and optimizer comparison.
The paper reports that SPSA simulation appeared close to the real distribution, but this is not a demonstrated quantum advantage.
